Definition: probably of Hebrew origin (compare H5716); Addi, an Israelite:--Addi.
BiblicalUsage: Addi shows up once, in Luke's genealogy of Jesus, as the son of Cosam and the father of Melchi. Luke lists him without a story of his own, one link in the long chain that runs from Adam to Jesus; Luke's genealogy is the whole of his story, with no fuller profile beyond it.
TheologicalSignificance: A name like this carries no teaching of its own, and I won't pretend it does. Its weight is the weight of the genealogy itself: Jesus was born into a real human line, with real ancestors whose names Luke bothered to record.
